subject: Boundary claim packaging and annotated topology — intake for SIG/CAIQ
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: topology + narrative for SOC2/SIG intake

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick chat this morning. We're starting the SIG/CAIQ intake for our procurement review and need a concise set of artifacts from Redwood covering Private and Dedicated deployment isolation and control-plane boundaries. To keep compliance moving, could you provide the following by EOD Tuesday (PST)?

- An annotated topology diagram showing Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated (reserved pools) demarcation, including control-plane endpoints and where customer data persists.
- A short narrative (~1 page) describing the isolation model (control plane vs data plane, routing/peering behavior, egress controls, and fallback behavior).
- A reachability/ACL excerpt or example firewall rules showing how tenant traffic is scoped.
- Any SOC2/SIG-friendly evidence IDs (diagram version, author, timestamp) so we can reference them in the questionnaire.

Attachments are fine; a single ZIP is perfect. Also note: we may need a few clarifying Qs after review.

Appreciate it — this will unblock our security SME.

Best,
Sarah Patel
Security Integration Lead
Acme Cloud

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: topology + narrative for SOC2/SIG intake

Hi Sarah — thanks for the list and timeline. We can provide a focused package that maps directly to SIG/CAIQ expectations. Tentative plan: deliver a single ZIP containing an annotated topology (PNG + Visio), a 1-page narrative PDF, a reachability matrix CSV, and an index file that gives artifact IDs for auditing.

Quick Qs to align expectations:
- Do you need VLAN/subnet-level diagrams or is service-level demarcation sufficient for your SME?
- Will the reviewer need specific egress NAT examples or a representative rule set is fine?

We aim to deliver a first pass by Tuesday EOD PST. If that timeline is tight we can prioritize the annotated diagram + narrative first and follow up with the ACL excerpts.

I'll loop in Kimberly and Ben to collect artifacts.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(Attachment placeholder: request_summary.txt)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: topology + narrative for SOC2/SIG intake

Team 0Kimberly/Ben1, can you own this intake for Acme? Below are the deliverables and suggested owners. Deliver to me by Mon EOD so I can QA and send to Acme by Tue.

Ask breakdown:
- Kimberly: Annotated topology diagram (Private vs Dedicated demarcation, control-plane endpoints, data persistence points). Deliver both PNG and a Visio/diagram source. Include artifact metadata (version, author, date).
- Ben: Reachability/ACL excerpt + firewall rule examples and a short paragraph describing egress handling (NAT, egress proxies, logging). Also capture a service-to-subnet mapping table for the review.
- Marissa (me): QA + narrative write-up; bundle into ZIP, create index.txt with artifact IDs and a short mapping to SIG/CAIQ questions.

Notes: Keep the narrative neutral and factual (avoid wording about 'guarantees'); highlight where customers can request additional isolation (VPC peering, private deployments). Also include how the control plane is logically separated and our fallback model when dedicated capacity is unavailable.

Kimberly/Ben 1 could you reply here with ETA and list of files you'll attach? If there are any sensitive snippets (e.g., firewall configs with internal IPs) redact them and replace with representative examples.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: topology + narrative for SOC2/SIG intake

Marissa 0 attaching first pass.

Files included (zipped):
- boundary_claim_pack_v1.zip (contains: annotated_topology_v1.png, annotated_topology_v1.vsdx, reachability_matrix_v1.csv, egress_examples_v1.txt, artifact_index_v1.md)

Highlights:
- The annotated topology shows both Private (customer VPC with dedicated connectors + optional on-prem private control plane endpoint) and Dedicated (shared Redwood GPU pools with tenant isolation via namespace + overlay). Control-plane endpoints are labeled with service roles and region tags.
- reachability_matrix_v1.csv includes a minimal set of ACL examples and explicit notation of "representative" IP ranges (redacted).
- artifact_index_v1.md enumerates artifact IDs and maps them to common SIG/CAIQ assertions (e.g., network segmentation, control-plane partitioning).

ETA: I can incorporate feedback and push v2 Monday morning.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(Attachment placeholders: boundary_claim_pack_v1.zip, annotated_topology_v1.png)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: topology + narrative for SOC2/SIG intake

Hi Sarah,

Attached is a first-pass package for your SIG/CAIQ intake (boundary_claim_pack_v1.zip). Summary of contents:
- annotated_topology_v1.png (diagram with control-plane/data-plane demarcation and artifact metadata)
- reachability_matrix_v1.csv (representative ACLs; sensitive IPs redacted)
- egress_examples_v1.txt (NAT/proxy patterns and logging endpoints)
- artifact_index_v1.md (maps files to SIG/CAIQ assertions and includes artifact IDs for traceability)

Link to a preview folder: https://drive.google.com/redwood/driveid-boundary-pack-v1

We expect to iterate once your SME reviews and sends any clarifying questions. If useful, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Kimberly and Ben early next week to step through the diagram and the reachability matrix. Are you available Mon morning PST?

Also: please let us know whether your SIG submission requires per-service egress rules (we've provided representative examples but can export service-level rules if required).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(Attachments: boundary_claim_pack_v1.zip)
